subject: Refresh images in www folder during a session

messages.author: b419b3f42893b2f1
messages.subject: Refresh images in www folder during a session
parts:
First - please excuse misuse of terms, I'm sure this can be described in better ways.

I have a complicated app that renders a large number of data dense plots. To speed things up, I save the plots as PNGs in the app's www folder so that they can be loaded instantly the next time they are requested.

So, if plots for the selected data exists, I render a UI with tags$img to display the images. If the selected data hasn't been plotted before, the app first creates the plots and then displays them the same way.

This works well. However, I do allow the user to change some features of the plots and re-plot the data, overwriting the old versions of the plot PNGs. This also works, but the app needs to be restarted for the new version to be displayed in the app. I suppose the original versions are cached, why the new image files won't show up.

So my question is if there is a way to clear the cached versions of the images, and refresh with the new ones.

Many thanks!

messages.subject: Re: Refresh images in www folder during a session
parts:
Thanks Joe, I've been a bit reluctant to use renderImage, as my first attempts with it were significantly slower. Also, an other functionality in the app is to quickly be able to reorder the about 100 images displayed according to user input, by just re-rendering the ui. All this works really well with the current approach, but would (as I understand it) requore all images to be re-read each time if using renderImage.

So, if there is a way (even a convoluted one) to solve my issue without changing that part of my approach, that would be fantastic.

Many thanks again.

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Refresh images in www folder during a session
parts:
That makes sense.

The easiest way of "busting" a cache is by adding a query parameter with some randomness or a timestamp in it. So if your file is called a.png then you'd always request it with the URL "a.png?nonce={random-number-here}". The query parameter will be ignored by the server but it will prevent the browser from using the cache to fulfill the request.
